incidents.vector: Hackers exploited an SSRF vulnerability (CVE-2026-134624) to breach an N-able-hosted server supporting the Mail Assure and SpamExperts email security platforms.
incidents.impact: Caused a week of outages and damage to Mail Assure/SpamExperts services; N-able found no evidence of exploitation beyond the single compromised server. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and gave federal agencies until Thanksgiving to patch.

incidents.victim: LaLiga and affiliated Spanish football clubs
incidents.vector: Intrusion into a third-party technology platform providing digital fan services to LaLiga and several of its clubs between Nov. 14-16.
incidents.impact: Theft of fans' personal identification and contact details at LaLiga and at least five clubs (CD Eldense, Real Oviedo, Real Zaragoza, Córdoba CF, CD Leganés); passwords, banking and payment information reported not compromised.

incidents.vector: North Korean state-linked actors compromised a Binance DevOps engineer's laptop, reached a service container, and submitted unauthorized cryptocurrency withdrawals.
incidents.impact: Approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency stolen in under four hours on Oct. 29; DOJ has since filed to forfeit over $1.1 billion in laundered USDC, part of roughly $2.9 billion recovered to date.

incidents.vector: Unauthenticated attacker exploited a deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2026-129514) in hex.pm's Erlang external-term-format request parser to execute operating system commands.
incidents.impact: Actively exploited against the live hex.pm service on Nov. 23; the vulnerability has since been patched.

incidents.vector: Unattributed group evaded detection for years by exploiting the government's fragmented networks and lack of integrated monitoring.
incidents.impact: Tens of millions of government documents stolen over at least five years before the group was evicted from state administration networks.

incidents.vector: Security breach identified by USDA's internal security team; technical details not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Applications used to issue payments to American farmers taken offline for more than a week; agency reset passwords across all databases.

incidents.victim: Austrian Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs
incidents.vector: Hackers believed to have entered through a third-party provider running the ministry's official website.
incidents.impact: Theft of data on ministry staff; attack not yet publicly attributed to a specific actor.

incidents.vector: A China-linked actor used Cairn AI agents to autonomously discover and exploit a zero-day path-traversal flaw in an exposed open-source medical imaging application.
incidents.impact: Agents escalated from vulnerability discovery to root access on the server in about 11 minutes via a Python reverse shell; the same 48-hour campaign also made unsuccessful attempts against other university systems.

incidents.vector: Files hosted on the agency's file-sharing service were left exposed online.
incidents.impact: Unspecified government files leaked online for roughly three and a half months (Jul. 30-Nov. 12) before discovery.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a shared third-party provider used by all three companies.
incidents.impact: Limited data stolen from each company; breaches claimed by extortion group tracked as "n0n."

incidents.vector: Breach reportedly caused by an AI tool; technical details not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Company investigating; scope of exposure not yet confirmed.

incidents.vector: Customer data left exposed online due to inadequate access controls.
incidents.impact: Exposed transcripts included transcriptions of law-enforcement body-camera footage.

incidents.victim: Federal Bureau of Investigation (National Crime Information Center)
incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion into the FBI's National Crime Information Center database; details withheld pending an active investigation.
incidents.impact: Second breach of FBI systems this year, following the September ShinyHunters attack on its HR recruiting portal; scope of data accessed has not been disclosed.

incidents.victim: GL.iNet customers (travel routers, IP KVM devices)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote-management service to install backdoors, disguised as a "crond" process, on customer devices.
incidents.impact: Backdoors deployed on an unspecified number of internet-connected routers and KVM devices; GL.iNet blocked the attack path and released firmware fixes.

incidents.vector: Attackers used authentic credentials leaked by a third party to access the Rackspace Spot cloud-resource marketplace.
incidents.impact: Kubernetes secrets stolen from customer accounts; attackers deployed unauthorized pods in affected cloud environments.

incidents.victim: Financial services, healthcare and legal organizations in the U.S., UK and Australia
incidents.vector: Com-affiliated actors (including Bling Libra/ShinyHunters) used vishing calls impersonating IT support to direct employees to adversary-in-the-middle proxy pages that harvested credentials and MFA approvals, followed by automated exfiltration from Microsoft 365, OneDrive and SharePoint.
incidents.impact: Sustained data-theft and extortion campaign active since August 2026, including exfiltration of tens of millions of CRM/recruiting records at some victims; attackers threaten regulatory reporting and leak publication to pressure payment.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized third party gained access to a database associated with McDonald's Japan's official mobile app.
incidents.impact: Exposed customers' purchase histories, IP addresses, internal customer ID numbers and mobile location data; names, emails, phone numbers and payment data were not affected.

incidents.victim: Instituto da Mobilidade e dos Transportes (IMT), Portugal
incidents.vector: Multiple cyberattacks against the Portuguese transportation agency; method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: All services temporarily suspended to protect data; no evidence of data theft found so far. Fourth Portuguese government body targeted in recent weeks.

incidents.vector: Company says the attacker used AI tooling to breach its systems; technical details not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Iceland's largest web hosting provider shut down services to protect customer data; tens of thousands of customer websites were taken offline.

incidents.vector: Cybersecurity incident affecting an IT platform used by repair shops to diagnose Nissan vehicles; initially mistaken for a routine technical outage.
incidents.impact: Platform down since Nov. 13; repair shops unable to diagnose vehicles, ship firmware updates, or replace lost key fobs.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack of undisclosed nature prompted the fundraising platform to take systems offline.
incidents.impact: Unclear whether customer or donor data was stolen; systems being restored gradually.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack of undisclosed nature against FDJ United's sports betting and online casino platforms.
incidents.impact: Unibet and several online casino sites taken offline; no technical details released.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack of undisclosed nature; technical details not released.
incidents.impact: Company reports systems recovered; no further details on data exposure provided.

incidents.victim: Microsoft Entra Connect Health customers (multiple tenants)
incidents.vector: A bug introduced via a July update to the Microsoft Entra Connect Health API allowed unauthorized read-only access to tenant metadata.
incidents.impact: Attacker collected administrator contact emails and tenant configuration data; Microsoft says no credentials, email content or documents were compromised. Fix deployed Nov. 19.

incidents.vector: Threat actor exploited a vulnerability in Microsoft Azure API Management (Classic tier) to target stored credentials and sensitive access tokens.
incidents.impact: Disrupted some internal services at Equinor; no evidence of data theft or alteration at either company. Norway's NSM says the underlying vulnerability affected organizations across multiple sectors and countries.

incidents.victim: 178+ websites, including BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom
incidents.vector: Attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into customer accounts, served from Optimizely's legitimate CDN under its own certificate.
incidents.impact: Malware delivered to visitors of at least 178 organizations' websites, stealing payment card data and swapping cryptocurrency wallet addresses; also attempted to deliver iOS/iPad exploit kits. Optimizely patched the flaw and remediated within 24 hours.

incidents.vector: Attacker used a cloud access key Barracuda had issued to a third-party AI service provider and failed to revoke, then deployed the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework to escalate access across internal network and cloud environments.
incidents.impact: Unauthorized access to Barracuda's cloud environment for roughly two days before detection and containment.

incidents.vector: The newly identified SilentAir group plants backdoors in telco infrastructure that run malicious SS7 and Diameter protocol commands.
incidents.impact: Collection of device data, subscriber location tracking, and interception of calls and SMS traffic against carefully selected targets; active since early 2025.

incidents.victim: 19 organizations including an industry standards body, a semiconductor manufacturer, a U.S. teachers' union, and a defense-policy think tank
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking attackers (tracked as CL-STA-1238) paired the open-source Cairn AI penetration-testing framework with Chinese AI models (Zhipu GLM, DeepSeek) to autonomously plan and execute 25 operations against 19 organizations, exploiting weak credentials and unauthenticated endpoints.
incidents.impact: Confirmed unauthorized access or data retrieval at 10 organizations, including exposure of more than one million member records, military and government identities, and creation of persistent administrator accounts in a production system.

incidents.victim: Government ministries in one Middle Eastern and four Southeast Asian countries
incidents.vector: Attacker injected malicious JavaScript into webmail portals and government web applications to run the "Falcon" (XG) browser-based C2 framework, which sideloads malicious Chrome extensions.
incidents.impact: Theft of passwords, emails, session cookies and communications from compromised ministries of foreign affairs, defense, interior and law enforcement agencies between March and May 2026.

incidents.victim: ~700 French retail stores, food factories, a slaughterhouse and blood banks; sites in nine European countries
incidents.vector: Attackers accessed internet-exposed refrigeration-system admin interfaces using known vulnerabilities and default credentials, switching units into defrost mode.
incidents.impact: Spoiled stock and tens of millions of euros in losses across roughly 700 French retail sites; French blood banks also affected. French officials attributed the October campaign to the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh unit within the Cyber-Electronic Command.
